framing: An observation is not a mathematical truth, so this layer declares NO axiom. Each entry is a Lean structure whose fields are the measured numbers and whose proof obligations are the inequalities the observation asserts; a theorem that needs an observation takes the structure as an argument, exactly as the scaling modules take AreaLaw and CubeLaw. #print axioms therefore still reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for every theorem in the development (lean/Delphi/Audit.lean). Status "empirical" is distinct from "proved": a reader may reject an entry, and the ledger says which eliminations were conditional on it.

nonVacuity.why: An inconsistent set of observations would let the checker eliminate every candidate, and that failure would look exactly like success. The witness instantiates every entry with the project's measured numbers at once; if two entries contradicted each other it would not type-check.
nonVacuity.mutation: lean/mutate.mjs: empirical-witness-outside-band moves a band so the measured value falls outside it, and the witness must then fail to compile.

entries.title: Isometry fails within a species
entries.statement: areaExponent < 2 and 1 < wingLoadingExponent, with the mass exponent in [2.90, 3.02].
entries.observation: Within one species, pectoral fin area grows as SL^1.834 and wing loading as SL^1.236 (mass as SL^2.981): fin area falls behind the isometric square and wing loading outruns the isometric first power, so a bigger fish of the same species is more heavily loaded than isometry predicts.
entries.source: physics/allometry.json (Davenport 1992, as the physics thread recorded it)

entries.note: the abstract calls growth in mass negatively allometric; 2.981 is just below the isometric 3

entries.quantity: lateral fin area vs standard length
entries.note: below the isometric 2: fins grow relatively smaller as the fish grows

entries.taxa: Exocoetus obtusirostris, one species, within-species regressions (the exponents are the three 'vs standard length' entries of the file)
entries.scope: Three separate regressions, no confidence intervals, and NOT mutually consistent: 2.981 - 1.834 = 1.147 against the fitted 1.236. That inconsistency is why C13 needs intervals, and it is the reason nine audit rows read "violated" rather than a defect of those theorems.
entries.usedBy: the flying-fish audit (lean/AUDIT-FLYING-FISH.md): the rows whose isometry hypotheses this observation contradicts
entries.rejectable: Reject it and the audit rows that read "violated" become "cannot evaluate"; nothing proved elsewhere changes.

entries.title: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
entries.statement: 2.90 <= b <= 3.02; hence for a weight following one power law, r^2.90 <= W(L2)/W(L1) <= r^3.02 when r = L2/L1 >= 1.
entries.observation: The 6 fitted field length-weight studies of 5 flying-fish species in the project's own table give exponents from 2.908 to 3.011.
entries.source: physics/length-weight.csv (FishBase length-weight list page, rows with a locality and n)

excluded.why: a male-only fit far below every other row; named here rather than silently dropped

entries.taxa: Cheilopogon atrisignis; Cheilopogon unicolor; Cypselurus poecilopterus; Hirundichthys affinis (female); Hirundichthys affinis (mixed); Hirundichthys oxycephalus
entries.scope: The 1 male-only row (Hirundichthys affinis, b = 2.208) is EXCLUDED and named: including it would widen the band to 2.21. Length types differ across rows (SL, FL, TL) and the FishBase page does not show the references. Eighteen further rows with b exactly 3.000 and n of 2 to 6 are unverified estimates and are not used.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and a scaled design's weight is unconstrained by the record; the exact cube law (C7b) still rules under isometry.

entries.title: Efficiency, cardiac output and arterial O2 lie in the measured teleost ranges
entries.statement: eta <= 0.15, oxycaloric <= 19.35 J/ml, cardiac output <= 0.075 ml/s and arterial O2 <= 0.21 ml/ml imply an aerobic ceiling of at most 0.0458 W.
entries.observation: No teleost in the ranges the physiology chain cites has a sustained aerobic ceiling above 0.0458 W at the measured mass (0.06 kg). This is what makes the C14 eliminations binding: they hold for every animal the measured record allows, not only for one choice of proxies.
entries.source: physiology/muscle.js (efficiency, oxycaloric), physiology/cardiac.js (cardiac output range), physiology/haemoglobin.js (blood O2 capacity), as cited in lean/eliminate/physiology-candidates.json

from.efficiency: efficiency: { value: 0.15, kind: 'proxy', species: 'Salmo salar (ventricular muscle)', source: 'gamperl2021: efficiency of ventricular muscle ~15% in salmon (7% in char); trout ventricle 15-25% (Harwood et al. 2002, cited there). No fetched value for fish skeletal muscle, so cardiac muscle is used.'
from.oxycaloric: oxycalorific_J_per_mgO2: { value: 13.54, kind: 'secondary', source: 'gerry2014 (Fig. 1 legend): "oxycaloric value of 13.54 J mg-1 O2" citing their ref. 89' }
from.cardiacRange: Q_range_ml_min_kg: { value: [20, 75], kind: 'secondary', species: 'O. mykiss', source: 'gerry2014 Discussion: ventral aortic flow-cuff values ~20 at rest to ~75 ml/min/kg maximum (citing refs)' }
from.haemoglobinCapacity: cap_ml_per_ml: { value: (4 * 0.9 * 22.4) / 1000, kind: 'proxy', species: 'Oncorhynchus mykiss', source: 'derived from rummer2015 Table 1 [Hb] 0.9 mM per tetramer (Hct standardised to ~25%): 4 x 0.9 mmol/l x 22.4 ml/mmol = 0.0806 ml O2/ml' }

entries.taxa: Every value is a PROXY from another teleost: Salmo salar ventricular muscle (efficiency), Lutjanus apodus and Oncorhynchus mykiss (cardiac output), Oncorhynchus mykiss (blood O2). No Exocoetidae physiology exists in this project.
entries.scope: The bound is an upper bound at one mass, and the cardiac output ceiling is the maximum of a secondary range (20 to 75 ml/min/kg, gerry2014 Discussion). It bounds SUSTAINED AEROBIC power only: burst power on white-muscle stores is outside it, and that is what a flying fish is understood to use. Scaling it to another mass requires the cardiac output per kg, not this number.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and C14 still rules, but only on the particular proxies a candidate commits, not on every teleost.

entries.title: Gills do not ventilate in air
entries.statement: uptakeInAir = 0; hence over a flight of duration t the mean aerobic power is at most E S / t for an O2 store S.
entries.observation: O2 uptake is zero while airborne, so airborne aerobic work is paid for out of the store carried into the air, and the airborne aerobic ceiling falls as the flight lengthens.
entries.source: physiology/index.js (the chain sets uptake to zero in air) and its self-test, where the store drains
entries.taxa: A property of the gill as a water-breathing organ, not of a species; the chain applies it to its flying-fish model.
entries.scope: Bounds the AEROBIC part only, and takes the store and the oxycaloric equivalent as inputs: neither is measured for Exocoetidae here. Cutaneous and buccal exchange in air are not modelled, and burst (anaerobic) power is outside it.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and the airborne ceiling is whatever the circulation can deliver, i.e. C14 with no time limit.

entries.title: The observed pectoral/SL range
entries.statement: 0.406 <= pectoral/SL <= 0.823 for a measured specimen; a design outside the range is above or below it.
entries.observation: Across 49 flying-fish specimens, pectoral fin length over standard length runs from 0.406 to 0.823, median 0.687 (standard lengths 1.68 to 24 cm).
entries.taxa: Beloniform museum specimens: flying fish only in this entry (the file also records flying halfbeaks 0.175-0.388, halfbeaks 0.115-0.177, needlefish 0.071-0.106).
entries.scope: A statement about the RECORD. A design outside the range is outside everything measured, which is weaker than impossible, and no theorem here says such a fish cannot exist. Preserved museum specimens, lengths only: no mass, no fin area, no glide data. It is deliberately NOT a constraint in the ledger, so that nothing is ever reported as eliminated by it; it is a flag in the Design Studio.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and the Studio loses a provenance flag; no verdict anywhere changes.

entries.title: "required for" is never propagated down part_of
entries.statement: No row of the map whose link type is "required for" is derived by propagating a link down a part_of edge.
entries.observation: Not an observation at all: a rule this project adopted for building the genotype map (the hub's idea-gp-propagation-rules). A gene required for a whole need not be required for each part.
entries.source: the genotype map's own propagation_rules (genotype/map.vetted.json) and the hub's adopted rule
entries.taxa: none: a rule about the map, not about animals
entries.scope: A convention, so it can be wrong only in the sense of being a bad choice. Labelled as such wherever it appears, and it licenses no biological conclusion.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and the map may carry downward "required for" links; the closure check (G2) then propagates an edit to more nodes, not fewer.

entries.title: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
entries.statement: death_hpf <= scored_hpf implies the phenotype cannot be scored in a living animal.
entries.observation: Two levers in the project's own intervention table state both times: ezh2 dies at 48 hpf, the stage at which its fin absence is scored, and wls dies by 12 dpf while the ray parameters exist only from 45 dpf.
entries.source: genotype/interventions.json (the genotype thread's own lethality notes, quoted in the value)

evaluated.quote: LETHAL: 'die around 2 days post fertilization' / 'They die at 48 hpf'. The animal dies at the same stage at which the fin phenotype is scored, before any fin skeletal differentiation.

LETHAL BEFORE THE RAY PARAMETER EXISTS: 'The mutants fail to develop swim bladders and die by approximately 12 dpf.' Lepidotrichia are not formed by then, so no ray length, segment or branching value can be measured in this allele, and the effect_size value is null for that reason. Even fully rescued mutants 'did not survive to adulthood'.
evaluated.conversion: death "by approximately 12 dpf" = 288 h; the ray parameters exist only from Juvenile:Days 45-89, taken as 45 dpf = 1080 h

notEvaluated.why: the genotype thread records lethality as free text (58 rows say "not reported"); only rows that state BOTH a time of death and a scoring stage in hours are instantiated here, and no time is parsed out of prose beyond those two

entries.taxa: Danio rerio (zebrafish) alleles and treatments; nothing here is measured on a flying fish.
entries.scope: Only the 2 rows that state both a death time and a scoring stage in hours are instantiated. the genotype thread records lethality as free text (58 rows say "not reported"); only rows that state BOTH a time of death and a scoring stage in hours are instantiated here, and no time is parsed out of prose beyond those two Lethality of a homozygote says nothing about a heterozygote, a mosaic, a conditional allele or a rescue, and a lever lethal in zebrafish may not be in another species.
entries.rejectable: Reject it and a design may claim a phenotype from a lever whose animal does not reach the stage; nothing proved elsewhere changes.

entries.status: not an empirical entry: already proved
entries.title: A part cannot appear before its precursor
entries.statement: Every develops_from edge goes strictly later in stage, and the relation is acyclic.
entries.observation: The stages are data (ZFIN); the ordering is a THEOREM about that data, certified by a kernel evaluation on the fin subtree. Restating it as an empirical hypothesis would weaken a theorem into an assumption, so it is not in this layer.
entries.taxa: Danio rerio anatomy (ZFA), joined to the blueprint by cross-reference
entries.scope: See the law genotype-developmental-ordering in lean/laws.json.
entries.rejectable: The ZFIN stage order is the assumption; reject it and the certificate says nothing.
